scope: B visibly reduces the sharp outer-lid fold in the frontal macro. Both candidates add collision pairs in evaluated held blink poses.

gains: The crease persists on the isolated skin, and B visibly softens the temporal fold.
B reduces the two measured outer ray steps at pixels 204,342 and 436,342 from 87.97 and 110.44 degrees to 28.71 and 52.77 degrees.
The r498 cheek and r497 hair are preserved.
defects: A provides a smaller visual change.
The closed crease remains noticeable in the oblique and profile.
Both native candidates fail the discrete collision gate.

nextAction: Retain r498 B as the working source. Use the positive-X frame 37 skin-pair witnesses and the combined iris-shell pair in A to define separate outer surface and inner clearance domains. Solve a blink-shape correction jointly against neutral and held gaze poses, with fixed margin and signed ocular clearance, rather than reusing one neutral depth offset through every gaze pose.
inheritedRetirements: Preserve all prior hair retirements. The r499 neutral-only depth correctives have been rejected because of measured collision regressions. Preserve the useful fixed-camera fold attribution and exact polygon witnesses. No adopted complete appearance or score increase.
